title: Carnival people's training and the early hotel problem for musicians
summary: Carnival performers taught the young musicians hygiene and discipline; he says musicians and ballplayers were turned away from hotels because of their trade.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Just traveling around all over the United States.
In one particular portion of the United States?

No particular. I had the advantage of being on these carnivals and circuses and what-have-you, you know, and the show break up. You don't know what's happening. I do remember that we were connected with peoples that had foreign intrigue. These peoples - Hungarians, Lithuanians and what-have-you, trapeze artists and what-have-you - they taught us how to eat, they taught us how to think, they taught us everything, they taught us personal hygiene, they taught us everything, you see. And like I said, you had to be a good 25 before you took a drink, not 21. See, they just didn't allow that. You could not go on the town because if you was on a carn y, which is a carnival, you got to go find some place to stay. They didn't have the motels then... because you must remember, Milt, when we came to New York in 1936 the New York Giants was still staying at the Braddock Hotel. Until Mr. Joe DiMaggio came in and the man, Mr. Edison, Marie Cramer's brother, liked Joe DiMaggio, baseball players did not stay in reputable hotels. [You're] a baseball player?

You're a musician? What? You're with a carnival? Out! You know how difficult it was for us to stay and it had nothing to do with color. It was just you were identified. with a semi-pro team, Oh, you're a baseball player? I don't care what you was playing with. I don't care if you was a major leaguer. All the antics of Ty Cobb and people; everybody knows what those people were or what Babe Ruth did. Well, they were big stars; they could get away with things. But a kid today - he'd look like Little Lord Fauntleroy with what those people did. You see, but he was a big star.
